title: Give Claude your real context
principle: If you’re designing a feature for an existing app or website, connect GitHub so Claude can fetch your components and existing screens and use them as a starting point—with a few tries it can recreate existing designs with pretty high fidelity. Web search and MCP connections work in Claude Design too when the design depends on outside information.
procedure: Connect the real repo (GitHub) or paste the component paths that matter.
Point at existing screens/routes for the feature area before asking for net-new UI.
Require the model to name which components it will reuse.
Use web search / MCP when the design depends on outside facts (pricing, regs, sports data).
Iterate a few times comparing against production screenshots—not against memory.
examplePrompts: I connected our GitHub repo. Pull the relevant components and existing screens for <feature area>. Redesign <flow> starting from those real patterns—match our component vocabulary before proposing net-new UI.

Open these production screenshots + the components listed in <paths>. List mismatches between the redesign draft and our real patterns. Prefer reuse over invention; propose at most one net-new component with justification.
tips: Real components beat imagined design systems when shipping into an existing app.
Nate notes high fidelity is reachable “with a few tries,” not one shot.
Web search and MCP are first-class when the brief depends on outside information.

antiPatterns: Designing a feature in a vacuum beside the real app.
Describing the design system in prose instead of linking sources of truth.
One-shot redesign with no production comparison.
checklist: Reuse list written before net-new components.
promptWhy: Repo-as-context beats describing your design system from memory.
Screenshot+path audit catches parallel invented systems early.

avoidWhen: Designing a feature in a vacuum beside the real app.
inputs: A concrete user problem and the current artifact
Constraints, existing behavior and source attribution to preserve
agentContract.output: A bounded application of “Give Claude your real context” with before/after evidence and remaining limitations.
agentContract.recipe:
1. Connect the real repo (GitHub) or paste the component paths that matter.
2. Point at existing screens/routes for the feature area before asking for net-new UI.
3. Require the model to name which components it will reuse.
4. Use web search / MCP when the design depends on outside facts (pricing, regs, sports data).
5. Iterate a few times comparing against production screenshots—not against memory.
acceptance: Show the before/after artifact and explain how “Give Claude your real context” improves the named user task.

stateRequirements.responsive: Check 390px and desktop plus 200% zoom; preserve reading order, wrap long text and keep actions reachable.
stateRequirements.accessibility: Use semantic headings and native controls, visible labels and focus; normal text contrast at least 4.5:1.
stateRequirements.keyboard: Complete the primary action using Tab, Shift+Tab, Enter and Space; no pointer-only information or focus trap.
stateRequirements.reducedMotion: Remove nonessential movement; preserve all state and information without waiting for animation.
stateRequirements.loading: Show pending feedback only during real work; retain context and allow navigation away.
stateRequirements.empty: Distinguish no content from no matching results; explain how to proceed or reset filters.
stateRequirements.error: Explain the failed action, retain user input and offer recovery; never claim success on failure.
stateRequirements.interruption: A newer action wins; cancel or ignore stale results and keep controls responsive.
stateRequirements.stateChange: Announce important results politely without moving focus unexpectedly.

compatibility.rule: Start with one technique. Add at most one companion for a distinct unsolved problem; candidates are suggestions, not verified compatibility.
conflicts: Two techniques changing the same visual role require an explicit winner.
Do not combine multiple entrance or attention effects on one target.
Aesthetic subtraction must not remove semantics, feedback or attribution.
compatibility.stop: Stop when the named task is clearer and acceptance evidence is recorded; do not add polish without a problem.
